features.description: Local action backend with the trust-boundary controls: a localhost-bound action endpoint protected by a per-session auth token, strict origin restriction, and CSRF protection, exposing ONLY a command allowlist bound to operator_bucket actions (approve/request/reject for a named gate; triage apply --safe for auto_safe). No arbitrary command path. This is the gate that keeps the executor from becoming a general shell.
steps: Bind the action endpoint to localhost; issue a per-session auth token the served console must present
Enforce origin restriction + CSRF protection on every action request
Define the allowlist: only named-gate decisions and auto_safe apply; reject anything else
Tests: unauthorized/cross-origin/forged requests are refused; only allowlisted actions reach an executor
features.acceptance: The local action backend accepts only authenticated, same-origin, CSRF-protected requests for allowlisted operator_bucket actions; everything else is refused. Verified by tests proving unauthorized, cross-origin, and forged requests are rejected, and that no path reaches arbitrary command execution.

features.description: Browser-originated gate decision: the operator console can approve / request-changes / reject a LIVE gate directly, with an explicit confirmation step, routed through F001's allowlist, writing an evidence record atomically (the decision and its evidence commit together or not at all).
steps: Wire approve/request/reject buttons to the F001 backend for a named live gate
Require an explicit confirmation step before the mutation
Tests: a confirmed approval clears the gate and records evidence atomically; a refused/cancelled one mutates nothing
features.acceptance: A human can approve/request-changes/reject a live gate from the console with explicit confirmation, the action commits atomically with its evidence, and a cancelled action mutates nothing. Verified by tests on real gate state.

features.description: Browser-originated safe-tier apply: the console can run the dry-run then confirm the auto_safe apply directly, driving the 2026-06-06-001 F005 engine through F001's allowlist, with the same dry-run-first / confirm / atomic-evidence rules. Still auto_safe only; still refuses creds/approvals/project mutations.
steps: Wire a dry-run-then-confirm safe-tier affordance to the F001 backend, driving the F005 engine
Preserve auto_safe-only scope and the hard refusals
Tests: dry-run mutates nothing; confirm applies only auto_safe + records evidence; non-safe items refused
features.acceptance: The console can dry-run and then confirm-apply the auto_safe tier, driving the F005 engine via F001, with atomic evidence and auto_safe-only scope preserved. Verified by tests proving dry-run is side-effect-free, confirm applies only auto_safe + writes evidence, and non-safe items are refused.

features.description: Integrity under failure: idempotency keys so a double-click or retry never double-applies; audit-log integrity (append-only, tamper-evident) so every browser-originated action is provably recorded; failure recovery so a partial action leaves a clean, resumable state; and a stale-tab guard — each action carries the model fingerprint it was issued against, and the backend refuses if the world has moved on.
steps: Idempotency keys on every action; replays are no-ops
Append-only, tamper-evident audit log of browser-originated actions
Failure recovery: a partial/interrupted action leaves a clean resumable state
Stale-tab guard: refuse actions whose issued-against model fingerprint no longer matches
Tests: double-submit is idempotent; tampering is detectable; an interrupted action recovers; a stale-fingerprint action is refused
features.acceptance: Browser-originated actions are idempotent (no double-apply), provably logged (tamper-evident), recoverable after interruption, and refused when issued against a stale model fingerprint. Verified by tests covering double-submit, tamper detection, interrupted-action recovery, and stale-tab refusal.

features.description: Embedded terminal — PTY↔WebSocket bridge (pty_bridge): stdlib RFC-6455 handshake + frame codec + login-shell PTY pump + resize. No new deps.
features.acceptance: Handshake matches the RFC-6455 vector; frames round-trip including masked/extended/partial; a shell runs a command and is reaped on socket close; resize control frame applies.

features.description: Embedded terminal — serve integration: threaded server + guarded /pty + /terminal/session behind --enable-terminal; loopback + Origin + per-serve token.
features.acceptance: Off-by-default → /pty 404 + session enabled:false; wrong/no token → 403; foreign Origin → 403; loopback-only enforced; good token+origin → a live shell over the real serve handler.

features.description: Embedded terminal — governance: audit log line when armed, NO auto-enable from config/build, threat-model doc.
features.acceptance: terminal_audit_line names local shell + cwd + unrestricted; serve_start defaults enable_terminal=False; build() exposes no enable_terminal param; threat model documents the residual local-token risk.

features.description: Embedded terminal — frontend dock: always-visible xterm dock; visible warning + scope when armed; honest off-hint when not.
features.acceptance: Dock renders regardless of state; armed → '⚠ Terminal enabled · local shell · <repo> · unrestricted commands' + 'Shell: <repo> · session active'; disabled → off-hint with --enable-terminal, no warning.
